On the 20th of July 2026, there was an issue with the wake-up functionality affecting Personal Editions. This occurred in all three regions \(US East, Europe and Asia Pacific\).  
Users were unable to wake up their environments from hibernation. When attempting to wake up the environments, they either remained in hibernation or moved to a "waking up" state indefinitely, preventing access to applications.  
This was caused by an issue in how our backend systems processed environment status updates. Due to messages being processed out of order, some environments' internal state was incorrectly reverted to 'hibernated' after they had already woken up successfully, even though the environment itself remained accessible on the backend. This caused the ODC Portal to keep showing an inaccurate 'hibernated' or 'waking up' status, and repeated wake-up attempts did not resolve it since the underlying state kept getting overwritten.  
We identified the root cause on the 21st of July and deployed a code fix to correct the state synchronization. The fix started to be rolled out to all regions on 22nd of July and completed by the 23rd of July. All affected environments were woken up successfully.  
We are implementing additional state verification checks to ensure the ODC Portal and backend systems remain in sync. A full technical review is underway to identify similar synchronization gaps across other features.  
We apologize for any disruption caused and thank you for your patience.

j44j3fx9cspr.body:
On October 20th, our cloud service provider experienced a high error rate and latency in the N. Virginia Region, which temporarily affected some of our internal tools and caused service disruption for O11 and ODC customers.  
The issue was first reported at 08:37 UTC\+1 for ODC, affecting access to ODC Studio and running applications in ODC Portal.  
O11 had the first report at 08:54 UTC\+1. Cloud customers weren't able to access their Service Centers, IdP Authentication started to present some failures, CloudWatch started to fail, and several other symptoms were felt, since it affected several networking resources, including 503 error messages.  
Customers also experienced delays or interruptions using our services, including Forge, MABs, Licensing Registration, and accessing our Portals and telephony services.  
Our Support and Operations teams closely monitored the situation throughout the day, providing continuous updates to affected customers and coordinating internally to restore full functionality as quickly as possible.  
By 14:06 UTC\+1, it was reported that a full recovery of services had been achieved, and customers began confirming that their services were operating normally. However, later in the afternoon, around 16h32 UTC\+1, we started again receiving reports of connectivity issues, affecting O11 customers. During the recovery process, due to latency errors, several customers experienced network connectivity issues. Our teams continued providing updates and ensured all systems remained stable.  
AWS confirmed that all its services returned to normal operations by 23:01 UTC\+1. This disruption affected 142 AWS services, causing a direct impact on OutSystems services. They determined that the incident was caused by DNS resolution issues affecting DynamoDB. Following this, EC2 instance launches and Network Load Balancer health checks were also impacted, which in turn affected connectivity for Lambda, DynamoDB, and CloudWatch. 

We apologize for any inconvenience caused and thank you for your patience.

Connection attempts returned an error stating, "Mentor couldn't connect. Please go online and try again." Deployed applications and other ODC Studio functionality were not affected._  
_As part of planned regional infrastructure work, Mentor connection requests from affected environments began being sent to a new regional destination. The services needed to handle those requests had not yet been deployed there, so every connection attempt failed. The change was applied ahead of those services becoming available._  
_The issue was detected through customer reports. Automated monitoring did not alert on it, because connection requests were being sent to a destination where the supporting service was not yet running, so no failure signals were generated for our monitoring to detect._  
_To restore service, we reversed the configuration change on a single environment and confirmed that Mentor connected successfully, then applied the same reversal across all affected environments. We verified recovery with each of the customers who had reported the issue._  
_To prevent recurrence, the regional infrastructure work will not resume until all dependent services are available in the region. We are strengthening the validation applied before configuration updates of this kind, so that a change cannot be made ahead of the services it depends on. We are also reviewing our monitoring so that failures of this type are detected automatically rather than through customer reports._  
_We apologise for any disruption caused and thank you for your patience._
